standard: ISO 261/262 (pitch series); tap drills per the published machinist tables named in sources
sources: AIMS Industrial Supplies, "Tap Drill Size Chart: Metric & Imperial Thread Sizes", https://aimsindustrial.com.au/blogs/product-guides/blog-threading-tap-metric-imperial-size-chart (read 2026-08-13)
notes: The pitch column is ISO 261/262 and is not in dispute. The tap drill column is a SHOP number, not a standard: it is the stock drill nearest the theoretical d - P for a nominal ~70-75% thread engagement, and published tables round it differently. Only rows where both sources print the same drill ship.

Casualties of that rule, recorded so nobody thinks they were forgotten: M3.5, M14, M18 and M22 coarse, and the M12x1.5 / M12x1.25 / M6x0.75 fine rows, appear in one source only or with two different drills. Add them when a second source corroborates, not before.
tap_drill is the diameter to BORE for a cosmetic/tapped hole. It is NOT the radius to bore when fusing real thread geometry - see the CHEATSHEET rule about boring at root_radius for real threads.
